identity.title: The Dust and [C II] Morphologies of Redshift ∼4.5 Sub-millimeter Galaxies at ∼200 pc Resolution: The Absence of Large Clumps in the Interstellar Medium at High-redshift

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present deep high resolution (0.03$''$, 200 pc) ALMA Band 7 observations covering the dust continuum and [CII] $\lambda157.7$ $\mu$m emission in four $z\sim4.4-4.8$ sub-millimeter galaxies

distance_source.value: Coppin et al. 2009; De Breuck et al. 2014

question.value: Do z~4.5 SMGs show giant ~200 pc clumps in dust and [CII] at 0.03'' resolution, how do [CII] and dust sizes compare, and what drives the [CII] deficit?

evidence.quote: The data show that the rest-frame 160 $\mu$m (observed 345 GHz) dust emission is consistent with smooth morphologies on kpc scales for three of the sources.

evidence.quote: The two independent methods of estimating the gas masses result in masses agreeing within the uncertainties.

findings_qualitative.value: Three SMGs smooth at 0.03''; UDS 47.0 structure statistically consistent with smooth disk.

evidence.quote: We conclude that it is therefore not possible to rule out the hypothesis that all four SMGs in our sample are smooth exponential disks.

findings_qualitative.value: Core has lower L[CII]/LFIR and higher SigmaSFR than annulus in all four SMGs, indicating a local origin of the [CII] deficit.

evidence.quote: the core has lower $L_{\text{[CII]}}$/$L_{\text{FIR}}$ and higher star-formation rate surface density than the surrounding annulus

claims.hypothesis: Do z~4.5 SMGs contain giant ~200 pc dust clumps?
claims.experiment: 0.03'' Band 7 imaging and simulations of smooth exponential disks
claims.result: Three smooth; UDS 47.0 clumps at 3.9–5.4 sigma, ~70% consistent with smooth disk
claims.finding: No evidence for large clumps; smooth disks can appear clumpy

evidence.quote: the apparent structures seen for UDS 47.0 have significance levels of just $3.9-5.4\sigma$

claims.hypothesis: Is [CII] more extended than the dust continuum?
claims.experiment: Half-Gaussian fits to uv amplitudes plus literature comparison
claims.finding: [CII] is more extended than rest-frame 160 um dust

evidence.quote: The weighted mean of the [CII] to rest-frame 160 $\mu$m dust continuum size, including our four SMGs and the comparison sample, is $1.6\pm0.4$.

claims.hypothesis: Is the [CII] deficit due to local or global processes?
claims.experiment: Core vs annulus L[CII]/LFIR against SigmaSFR
claims.result: All four cores show lower ratio and higher SigmaSFR
claims.finding: Deficit consistent with local processes; cannot distinguish saturation vs G/n models

evidence.quote: It is not possible therefore at this stage to determine which of these models best explains the [CII] deficit.

why_this_method.value: Natural weighting used to recover as much extended emission as possible

evidence.quote: natural weighting (ROBUST $=2$) in order to recover as much of the extended emission as possible

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Clumps at 200 pc unlikely to be self-gravitating given typical SMG velocity dispersions

evidence.quote: This suggests that the clumps in UDS 47.0, if real, are unlikely to represent self-gravitating physical structures.

limitations_admitted.value: Sparse short-baseline coverage (LAS ~0.42'') resolves out [CII] and extended dust; [CII] detections only 2.7–4.7 sigma.

evidence.quote: such high-resolution data therefore have to be interpreted with care
